clue.text: Tolerated temperature in a bizarre botanical garden

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the tolerated-plus-temperature letters sit inside the word for bizarre

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or strange
to bore something is to endure or put up with it

explanation.surface: Someone put up with the heat inside a strange botanical garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, meaning odd, is dated British slang much loved by setters.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a garden devoted to growing and displaying trees for study.

clue.text: Dread flying snake

indicators.note: letters sent flying are scattered and land in a new order

parts.note: the word dread supplies the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: A frightening snake darting through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The adder is Britain's only venomous snake, a kind of viper.

clue.text: Renege on an earlier decision, and support new deal under pressure

indicators.note: in a down answer the reworked deal letters come beneath the pressure letter

parts.note: to back is to support

indicators.note: a new deal is the word deal made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the word deal supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone goes back on a decision, endorsing a fresh deal while under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to retreat from a position or commitment previously taken, an idiom from reversing on a bicycle.

clue.text: Long-tailed bird in way on river?

indicators.note: in a down answer the way sits on top of the river

parts.note: a road is a way
something that runs; a river runs, so it can be called a runner

explanation.surface: A long-tailed bird spotted on a path beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags river as a runner, i.e. a thing that runs, rather than a named river.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadrunner is a fast-running cuckoo of the American southwest with a long tail.

clue.text: Shake doctor heading for Lisbon in plane?

indicators.note: the doctor and the Lisbon initial go inside the tree

parts.note: the plane is a tree, as in London plane

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Lisbon contributes only its initial letter

explanation.surface: A medic trembles aboard an aircraft bound for Lisbon.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane looks like an aircraft, but it is the plane tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To tremble is to quiver or shake involuntarily.

clue.text: Slander bishop at hospital for medical treatment

parts.note: mud is damaging accusation, as in mud-slinging
taken as written

explanation.surface: Smearing a bishop who is in hospital being treated.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath in mineral-rich mud is a spa therapy for rheumatism and skin complaints.

clue.text: Daughter's after dainty material

indicators.note: the daughter comes after the word for dainty

parts.note: twee is British for affectedly dainty or quaint
D for daughter; the 's is 'is', joining it to after

explanation.surface: A daughter seeks out pretty, delicate fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, originally from Scotland.

clue.text: Go for a spin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a go is a ..., an opportunity to play
second meaning: to rotate or spin

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a drive out; split them and each names the same short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a person's go in a game and a rotation about an axis.

clue.text: Couple ultimately bound to run away to Gretna Green?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of couple

parts.note: the word couple gives only its final letter
to lope is to move with long bounding strides

explanation.surface: A couple finally determined to flee to Gretna Green to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was where English couples went to marry without parental consent.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run off secretly to marry, which Gretna Green is famous for.

clue.text: Out of order, nudge guy astride black recreational vehicle

indicators.note: the rearranged letters straddle the black letter, one part each side
letters out of order are jumbled into a new sequence

parts.note: these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A broken-down vehicle; someone shoves a man sitting on a black one.
explanation.definitionFit: A dune buggy is a light open car with big tyres, driven for fun on sand.

clue.text: Beginning to devour a tea in Vladimir's country cottage?

indicators.note: the beginning to a word is its first letter

parts.note: devour gives only its opening letter
taken as written
cha (char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: Starting to gulp a cup of tea at a Russian's country retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Vladimir stands for any Russian, which the question mark admits.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian holiday house in the countryside.

clue.text: Bedcover we'd ironed badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: these words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A quilt that we pressed poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down feathers, laid on a bed.

clue.text: Comic strip character close to Sweep stabbing nasty brute in back

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: the closing letter of Sweep pierces the scrambled brute

parts.note: the word brute supplies the letters to be scrambled

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

parts.note: Sweep gives only its final letter

explanation.walkthrough: Sweep is a British TV glove puppet, a dog, so the surface lives among children's characters.

clue.text: Rosemary, for one, in Father Brown

indicators.note: the letters lie inside the run of Father Brown

parts.note: the end of Father and start of Brown hold the answer

explanation.surface: Rosemary appearing as a character in a Father Brown story.

explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an example of a culinary plant used for flavouring.

clue.text: Current record about E.T. may be ill-advised

parts.note: in means fashionable, current
a disc is a record
re means concerning
taken as written

explanation.surface: Releasing a record about the film alien might be unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indiscreet means being careless about what one reveals, which is unwise.

clue.text: Play moderately slowly with stake money

definitions.note: a direction to performers, answered by the musical tempo marking

parts.note: and means with, together
the ante is the stake put up before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: Taking one's time over a game where money is staked.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the Italian musical marking for a moderately slow, walking tempo.

clue.text: Like one on the wagon missing imbibing can

indicators.note: imbibing means taking in, so the can goes inside

parts.note: absent is missing
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A teetotaller who goes missing after drinking a can.
explanation.definitionFit: On the wagon is an idiom for not drinking alcohol, i.e. abstaining.

clue.text: Suspend boxer, perhaps showing a sense of guilt

parts.note: to hang is to suspend
a boxer is an example of a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A boxer banned from fighting looks ashamed.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxer looks like a fighter, but it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangdog look is a shamefaced, guilty expression.

clue.text: One may be leaving Euston in blue coach

parts.note: to feel down is to feel blue
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: Someone departing a London station, sad, in a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Euston is a London terminus; British railways call trains leaving London down trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A down train runs away from the main London terminus, as any train leaving Euston does.

clue.text: Conspicuous foreigner in street

indicators.note: the foreigner is placed inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: an alien is a foreigner

explanation.surface: An outsider standing out on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: Salient means prominent or most noticeable.

clue.text: Row about stray dog

indicators.note: the row goes about, around, the straying word

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: An argument over a stray dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Row wants to be a quarrel; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrier is a breed type of small, lively dog originally used for hunting.

clue.text: Quite some distance? It may be between tee and green

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is quite a long distance

definitions.text: It may be between tee and green
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the mown stretch of a golf hole

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer into two words; the second reads it as one golfing term.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the closely mown strip from tee to putting green is this; idiomatically it also means a long distance.

clue.text: Mostly glowing about school chess champion

indicators.note: the clipped glowing word goes around the school abbreviation

parts.note: fiery means glowing

explanation.surface: A school's chess champion, nearly radiant with pride.

explanation.definitionFit: Bobby Fischer was a world chess champion, so the name is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Piece of information I came across in retirement

parts.note: taken as written

parts.note: met is came across

explanation.surface: A tidbit I picked up after I stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single detail or news report.

clue.text: Taken out of context, rapper added

indicators.note: the letters are lifted out from inside these words

parts.note: the end of context and start of rapper hold the answer

explanation.definitionFit: Extra means additional, more than the usual amount.

clue.text: Lawyer's dull speech unsettled court

indicators.note: unsettled letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the word court supplies the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An advocate's boring address upset the courtroom.

clue.text: Dieter's OK after port wine

clue.text: Instrument that's blown in Bow boozer, regularly

clue.text: Found his stable out of form

clue.text: Hera losing husband to another goddess

indicators.note: Hera loses a letter, so it is removed

parts.note: Hera is the Greek queen of the gods, wife of Zeus
taken as written

parts.note: a tirade is a rant
taken as written

clue.text: Queen mother leaving country for Hope's place

indicators.note: mother leaves the country's name, so her letters go
